questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Both academic and cultural factors were important for me in choosing my destination. I definitely had an urge to see something outside of Europe, and initially wanted to study in either Africa or South America. However, there were limited options there when I applied - and since I had always wanted to go to Australia that seemed the way to go. The fact that there would not be a language barrier for me in Australia (since I am fluent in English) was also a major contributing factor. 

I had heard heaps of good stuff about Melbourne. The University of Melbourne seemed like a good institution, and they offered quite a few very relevant and exciting subjects for me. There were also many exchange spots available for UCPH students, so it seemed like a safe choice.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was extremely lucky to find an affordable room relatively quickly. However, I know many people who were forced to spend a lot of money on accommodation - student housing in Melbourne is ridiculously expensive and practically ruled out for the vast majority of students, pushing most people in to the private housing market. Due to a massive cost-of-living and housing crisis is Melbourne (and most of Australia) rents are extortionately high as well, which can be a major challenge for students, particularly international students. For me, the ideal would have been to rent a room in a share house - many young people do this in Melbourne, but my experience was that most landlords do not take your application into consideration as they would prefer a longer term tenant (and a semester is relatively short in the grand scheme of things).
It is a major challenge finding affordable housing in Melbourne. However, sometimes you can get lucky. I used the website
Flatmates.com
, and I know other who found housing through the Facebook page FairyFloss Real Estate.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: For me, living off campus has definitely been a good experience. I was not into the idea of student housing - it often has a reputation of being a bit of a frat-house - so off campus accommodation was right for me. However, this means that you really have to actively engage in other social activities in order to meet new people, since you won't be rubbing shoulders with other students on a day-to-day basis outside of your classes. This is especially true if you don't live in a share house.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one first year course, one second year course and two third year courses. Generally I would say that the academic level is pretty similar to UCPH, but to be honest I wouldn't know since all of the courses I took while on exchange were elective and in a quite different field from the rest of my degree at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Each course has one lecture and one tutorial per week (in my case). This is quite different from the style of teaching at UCPH. The lectures are more "stiff", you basically just listen to the lecturer speak for a few hours, while the tutorials are supposed to be more engaging, as there are fewer students in each "team". Officially, you are expected to actively participate in every tutorial, however many seem to be uncomfortable speaking which does sometimes make tutorials slightly awkward.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is quite similar to Copenhagen in a number of ways, so it wasn't that difficult to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club - I recommend getting involved with the environment collective on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate how open and chatty Australians are!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared to spend more money than you thought you would. 
2. Prioritise your social life, it is really not that hard to pass your courses, and grades don't count towards your final degree.
3. Go on weekend trips!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about your studies. The semester goes by VERY quickly, so make the most of it while you're in Australia.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being part of the Socialist Alternative club on campus is definitely the most rewarding experience!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found that, while meeting lots of cool people, actually establishing real friendships is not a piece of cake. I did not hang around any other exchange students (only Aussies), so the classic "you're in it together" did not apply to me in terms of making friends. However, I am really pleased that I pushed through the initial phase, because now I have a bunch of lovely Australian friends.
